task.description: HARD GATE. Independently validate the test spec and both test files against REQ-024's 5 acceptance criteria and WF-02 Step 3b's checklist (a-e). TEST-DESIGNER reported a genuine concurrent-race test of the DB unique-index backstop via Task -- independently reproduce this yourself, don't trust the report. Also verify the two self-reported bugs (orphan-cleanup-timing bug, Map-iteration-order assumption bug) were genuinely fixed by reading the current code, not the narrative. TEST-DESIGNER also worked around a pre-existing gap (migration modules not in :test's elixirc_paths, requiring Code.require_file/1) -- confirm this workaround is test-file-scoped only and doesn't touch shipped code.
acceptance_criteria: at least one runnable test targets each acceptance criterion, no @tag :skip without a passing counterpart
no TODO: implement test left in the spec
tests are self-sufficient, no dependency on other tests running first, DB-backed tests clean up real Postgres state (tenants/schemas) via on_exit

result.summary:
Independently validated test/specs/REQ-024.md, registry_test.exs (28 tests), and json_schema_test.exs (45 tests) against WF-02 Step 3b's checklist (a-e) and the handoff's specific re-verification items. All checks pass.

(a-e) Read spec + both test files directly (not the producer's summary). All 5 ACs traced to concrete test cases: AC1->test case 1 (migration), AC2->cases 2-8 (register_type/2, including monotonicity + concurrency), AC3->cases 9-17 + JsonSchema's own 45 keyword tests, AC4->cases 18-22 (get_type/2), AC5->direct moduledoc inspection (independently re-read lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex lines 33-55 myself -- the '## JSON Schema validation library choice' section is present in substance as claimed). No @tag :skip, no 'TODO: implement test' anywhere (grepped both files + spec, zero matches). Fixtures use System.unique_integer/Ecto.UUID.generate() + per-test-fresh provisioned schemas, no shared hardcoded IDs. Tests self-sufficient: confirmed by running registry_test.exs isolated with 5 different seeds (101/202/303/404/505) -- 28/28 passed every time -- and running combinations that exclude/include each new file independently. No hardcoded secrets/connection strings (grepped for password/secret/postgres:// patterns, zero matches).

Item 2 (concurrency test): independently reproduced the concurrent-race test (registry_test.exs:409) 15 times in isolation with random seeds -- 15/15 passed, zero flakiness. Went further than the spec's own evidence: captured Ecto debug query logs across 5 additional runs and confirmed, every time, that BOTH tasks' `SELECT max(schema_version)` queries fired AND both proceeded to `INSERT` with the identical (name, schema_version) -- i.e. both tasks genuinely passed the application-level pre-check and it was the table's own unique index (via unique_violation?/2's constraint-name matching) that decided the winner, not sequential pre-check serialization producing the same external atom by coincidence. This closes a real ambiguity: {:error, :duplicate_event_type_version} is reachable via either the pre-check OR the DB-backstop path, so the test's external assertions alone could not distinguish them -- the query-log evidence does.

Item 3 (self-reported bugs): (a) orphan-cleanup-timing fix confirmed by direct code read -- on_exit/1 (registry_test.exs:168-176) is registered immediately after insert_tenant!() (line 158) and before provision_tenant_schema/replay_migrations (lines 178-181), so a failure in either later call still triggers cleanup. Independently ran `mix test test/letflow/event_store/` (73/73 passed) then queried Postgres directly myself (not the spec's claimed query): `SELECT nspname FROM pg_catalog.pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'tenant_%'` -> 0 rows; `SELECT count(*) FROM tenants WHERE slug LIKE 'req024-%'` -> 0 rows. Zero orphan state. (b) Map-iteration-order fix confirmed genuine, not lucky: the 'reports every violation' test (json_schema_test.exs, 'reports every violation, not just the first' describe block) now asserts the structurally-guaranteed required-before-properties order via `hd(failures(result))` and compares the full violation set via `MapSet.new(...)`, which is order-independent by construction -- mathematically cannot fail due to Map iteration order, unlike a pinned list assertion. Ran this file (and the whole registry event_store dir) repeatedly (~30+ total invocations across this validation session) with zero failures in json_schema_test.exs's own tests.

Item 4 (Code.require_file scoping): grepped lib/, priv/, and the whole repo for `Code.require_file` -- zero matches in lib/ or priv/; only appears in registry_test.exs, the two handoff files documenting it, and the spec itself. Confirmed test-file-scoped only.

Item 5 (independent re-run, real output quoted): `mix test test/letflow/event_store/` -> 'Result: 73 passed', reproduced multiple times, always clean. Full suite `mix test`: intermittently 233/234 or 234/234 across repeated runs (observed both outcomes). Root-caused this myself rather than accepting it at face value: the single intermittent failure is always `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatusTest`'s 'GET request issues no Ecto query' test (test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs:121) -- a pre-existing, ALREADY-TRACKED issue (docs/issues/ISS-0011.yaml, filed by RELEASE-VALIDATOR during REQ-022, status: open), caused by a global (non-pid-scoped) :telemetry.attach racing against concurrently-running async:true tests' own Ecto queries. Confirmed this is NOT caused by REQ-024's new tests: (1) running the full suite with test/letflow/event_store/ entirely excluded was 5/5 clean at the lower (161-test) baseline concurrency; (2) including registry_test.exs (async:false, DB-heavy) while excluding json_schema_test.exs was 4/4 clean, so the DB-backed new file is not the trigger; (3) including json_schema_test.exs (pure, zero-I/O, async:true, 45 tests) while excluding registry_test.exs reproduced the SAME pre-existing tenant_status_test.exs failure intermittently (~2 of 8-14 runs) -- meaning merely adding more concurrent async load (even zero-I/O tests) increases the probability of ISS-0011's pre-existing race window being hit; it is not a defect in REQ-024's own tests. Per docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md ('the current step's own PASS/FAIL verdict is unaffected by an incidentally-discovered issue') and core-directives.md's Unblock-Everything scope boundary, this does not block this gate. No new issue filed -- ISS-0011 already covers it exactly; re-observed and re-confirmed root cause independently rather than duplicated.

One additional non-blocking observation: `mix test test/letflow/event_store/` printed a compiler type-warning ('the following clause will never match') on registry_test.exs:654's `refute match?(nil, Registry.get_type(...))` -- the Elixir 1.20 set-theoretic type checker has proven get_type/2's own @spec never returns bare nil, making this specific defensive assertion type-provably redundant (the adjacent positive assertion on the same line already covers the behavior). Not a gate failure: it's a test-file-only warning (mix compile --warnings-as-errors only covers lib/, not test/), doesn't affect correctness or pass/fail, and the redundant assertion is harmless. Flagging for awareness only, not required to fix.
issues: Re-confirmed (not newly filed): docs/issues/ISS-0011.yaml (tenant_status_test.exs global-telemetry flakiness) is still open and was independently re-reproduced during this validation's full-suite runs; root-caused as unrelated to REQ-024 (see summary). No action needed from this gate.

Non-blocking: registry_test.exs:654 triggers an Elixir type-checker warning ('clause will never match') on a now-redundant refute match?(nil, ...) assertion, since get_type/2's own @spec already type-provably excludes nil. Cosmetic only; not a gate failure.
